identity.name: Tourbillon Souverain
identity.one_liner: F.P. Journe's first tourbillon wristwatch, built with a remontoir d'égalité to feed the escapement constant force and a 30-second vertical tourbillon carriage.

provenance_events.description: A unique tantalum-cased Tourbillon Souverain with a chrome-blue dial, made to echo the Chronomètre Bleu, sold for CHF 550,000 at the Only Watch 2015 charity auction.

narrative.story: The Tourbillon Souverain was part of F.P. Journe's founding collection when he began producing watches under his own name, pairing a tourbillon regulator with a remontoir d'égalité that resets every 30 seconds to deliver the escapement a constant, uniform amount of energy rather than the naturally decaying force of an unwinding mainspring. The gold movement construction, rather than the more common brass or German silver, was itself a departure most other tourbillon makers of the period did not follow.
narrative.collector_notes: This model was succeeded by the Tourbillon Souverain Vertical, which changed the tourbillon's orientation and the remontoir's visible position on the dial; collectors treat the two as related but distinct references rather than interchangeable.
